target.name: Clippership
target.founder: Nico Cymbalist, Luca Cymbalist, Kai Matsuka

methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Seed → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.5x) to $5M total raised proxy.

data.narrative:
Clippership is a Seed-stage ocean and maritime technology company that has raised $5M+ to date. The valuation analysis relies on a limited comp universe: three identifiable private peers (Standard Subsea, NetworkOcean, Albacore) and no direct public comparables in the sector, reflecting the nascent state of frontier maritime tech.

The stage-progression method is the primary applicable approach given the company's early funding history. Using the $5M total raised as a valuation proxy and applying a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical of Seed-to-next-stage progression yields an implied valuation of $12M. This single-method framework produces a median valuation of $12M, with a low-end estimate of $11M and a high-end estimate of $14M derived from sensitivity around the multiplier assumption.

The narrow valuation band of $11M–$14M reflects constrained analytical leverage. With only one primary method applicable and a three-company private comp set, the analysis carries material uncertainty around both the appropriate multiple and the relevance of peer trading multiples to Clippership's specific capital deployment and market traction. Investors should require additional diligence on the three private comparables' recent funding rounds, growth metrics, and business model alignment before anchoring to this range. The absence of public market data limits external validation of the private comp multiples themselves.
